12.2 Numerov returns the RAW (un-normalized) reduced radial wavefunction u(r); its overall scale is physically meaningless and set entirely by the unspecified first-step seed (u[0]=0 => solution is linear in u[1], so the seed only fixes scale, not shape). The original test compared the raw array, so it failed any correct-shape solution that used a different first-step convention: both deepseek models got the shape EXACTLY right (pro = gold x 1.385e9, constant to 1e-15; normalized == gold) and failed only on that arbitrary scale, because they bootstrapped u[1] with an O(h^4) Taylor step that blows up against the r->0 centrifugal/Coulomb singularity f(r0)~1.2e11. The downstream consumer 12.3 compute_Schrod normalizes via Simpson (gold 12.3 has integral u^2 dr = 1.0, verified on the gold target), so the scale is discarded immediately and never reaches anything physical. Fix: compare scale-invariant (normalize both sides by their L2 norm). This tests the physically-meaningful shape and dissolves the seed under-specification (no need to pin the seed). Numerov's contract (raw integrator) is unchanged; target/h5 unchanged; downstream golds unaffected (they normalize).
